Playing it safe how best to control your kids computer gaming

I normally just play some of the games along with my son. It's good father son time and it's fun. I figure it goes a lot farther than any other gimmicks I could try to "control" his gaming. I'd rather positively influence him by example.

Considering I don't believe there's really any correlation between negative child behavior and playing mature video games, I would have extremely lax oversight as to what game my child plays. I grew up all my life playing games without a regard to rating and so have many others without issue.

While I also don't think there is any meaningful correlation between negative child behavior and video games, the majority of children aren't yet ready to handle certain themes.
A good example would the The Last Of Us. By all rights this is an amazing game. However there are many very serious themes and elements that an 8 year old or a 12 year old just aren't ready to handle.

I have a 3 going on 4 year old. He loves playing video games with me. We play all sorts of action and adventure games but I avoid the zombie games and some other games as I know they will either give him fuel for nightmares or include themes he's not quite ready for yet. He will be ready for them one day but that's not today. I figure by being involved we get great time together and he gets some great games. It's also been amazing to see how much he can already read and pick up from the games.

From the article:

Games are becoming an integral part of childhood, and that’s no bad thing as they enrich our lives with powerful interactive stories, creative new worlds and fresh ways to play. But assessing value and violence remains complex and needs time and involvement from parents. A lack of information is really no longer an excuse to ignore the issues. Instead of simply believing the hype about gaming, parents should now engage with their kids to make informed, positive choices.

Thank you! This author totally gets it. With so many (middle-age or older) people alienated or confused by games, it's delightful to have somebody that actually understands.
